## Summary

The May 8 and November 7, 2026 guides describe stablecoin payments through Link for eligible US businesses and customers in supported countries. Stripe settles completed payments in the merchant’s Stripe balance in USD.

## Key Facts

- **Eligibility.** Eligible US businesses are subject to onboarding and restricted-business exclusions. Customers must be in a supported country. The payment must be one-time and on-session, presented in USD, and between 1 and 10,000 USD. The supported surfaces are Payment Links, Stripe Checkout and Elements. See November raw lines 8–36.
- **Activation and request access.** The guides say activating Link automatically enables stablecoin payments on supported integrations. Link guarantees the funds and says eligible existing integrations need no changes. November also shows a separate email form to request access. It gives no account-specific approval rule or explanation of how the form relates to automatic enablement. See November raw lines 11–36.
- **Wallets and settlement.** Customers choose a wallet, token and network from available options. The guides supply no comprehensive checkout wallet, token or network list. The November glossary names OUSD and USDC for Stripe stablecoin balances and USDC.e for transfers on Tempo. Those references describe balances and transfers. Completed Link payments settle in the merchant’s Stripe balance in USD, and the guide gives no merchant bank payout schedule. The separate direct Crypto product has its own accepted-token table, Billing support, business previews and settlement terms. See November raw lines 8–11 and [[stripe-stablecoin-payments]].
- **Testing.** Use a wallet funded on a blockchain testnet. See November raw lines 38–40.
- **Refunds and disputes.** Refunds go back as stablecoins to the customer’s original wallet. Disputes are unsupported. See November raw lines 65–69.

## Customer Flow

- **New customer.** The customer selects Crypto, enters their details and continues to Stripe Crypto, where they choose a wallet, authorize Stripe to interact with it, confirm the payment details and confirm through the wallet. Stripe then confirms successful payment. The customer automatically signs up for Link as part of this flow. See November raw lines 42–54.
- **Returning customer.** The customer selects their saved wallet and continues, receives prefilled details, confirms those details and confirms through the wallet. Stripe then confirms successful payment. Wallet selection, authorization, confirmation, saved details and Link signup are separate from Stripe’s successful payment confirmation. See November raw lines 56–63.

payments-link-stablecoins.Q1: The November 7 capture of https://docs.stripe.com/payments/link/stablecoins documents Link as the payment surface for eligible US businesses with onboarding and restricted-business conditions, and for customers in supported countries. Payment Links, Stripe Checkout and Elements support one-time, on-session USD payments from 1 to 10,000 USD. The guide says Link activation automatically enables the funding method and the funds guarantee means an existing eligible integration needs no changes. It separately shows an email request-access form and supplies no approval or universal requirement for that form (new raw lines 8-36). Testing requires a wallet funded on a blockchain testnet. New shoppers enter details, continue to Stripe Crypto, choose a wallet, authorize Stripe interaction and confirm payment details and wallet payment. They automatically sign up to Link. Returning shoppers use a saved wallet with details prefilled and still confirm in their wallet. Stripe then confirms successful payment. Only completed payments are described as settling in USD in the merchant's Stripe balance. Refunds go in stablecoins to the original wallet, and disputes are unsupported (new raw lines 38-69). The May 8 capture documents the same core payment limits, flows and outcomes (old raw lines 7-27 and 29-56). source-stripe-stablecoins-on-link.md now retains those core facts and scopes wallet, token and network choices to available checkout options. The new OUSD, USDC and Tempo USDC.e glossary wording covers Stripe stablecoin balances or transfers, and provides no Link checkout support matrix (new raw lines 8-11).
payments-link-stablecoins.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/link/stablecoins the November capture adds an email-based access-interest form and a glossary note describing OUSD and USDC for stablecoin balances and USDC.e for Tempo transfers. Step numbering and the disputes contraction are presentation changes (old raw lines 7-16 and 29-56, new raw lines 8-29 and 42-69). The form does not establish an approval event or displace the unchanged Link activation language. Keep both dated and preserve the May 8 capture in source-stripe-stablecoins-on-link.md. Correct the universal wallet, token and network wording there and on the reciprocal Link concept and index routes. Link-specific eligibility is supported customer countries, eligible US merchants, onboarding and restrictions, USD 1–10,000, one-time on-session, and Payment Links, Checkout or Elements (old raw lines 7-23 and new raw lines 8-36). The November direct Crypto overview separately describes its own token/network table, local-currency settlement, private previews and Billing support. The direct overview and the OUSD/USDC/USDC.e glossary do not extend Link's supported assets, geographies, recurring capability or settlement scope. Use a testnet wallet with testnet funds for testing. Wallet selection or confirmation and Link enrollment are distinct from Stripe-confirmed success and USD settlement into the merchant's Stripe balance, which gives no bank payout time. The captures do not identify a new server API or SDK version for Link. Stablecoin refunds return to the original wallet and disputes remain unsupported (old raw lines 25-56 and new raw lines 38-69).

concept_suggestions.proposed_markdown:
## Product Support

The direct Stripe Crypto product covers Checkout, Elements, Invoicing, Payment Links, Billing (invoices and subscriptions) and Connect (all charge types), subject to the product’s own eligibility. The November 2026 direct overview lists US business availability, private previews in the European Union, Hong Kong, Mexico and Switzerland, settlement in the merchant’s local currency in their Stripe balance, and a direct accepted-token table. Its USDC-on-Tempo listing applies to direct Crypto payments. See [[raw/stripe-payments-stablecoin-payments-2026-11-07|November 2026 direct Stripe Crypto overview]].

Stablecoins on Link is a separate funding path for eligible US businesses serving customers in supported countries. It covers one-time, on-session USD payments of 1–10,000 USD via Payment Links, Stripe Checkout or Elements, with USD settlement in the merchant’s Stripe balance on completion. The Link glossary names OUSD and USDC for balances and USDC.e for Tempo transfers. The Link guide supplies no comprehensive checkout token/network list. See [[source-stripe-stablecoins-on-link]].
warnings: Direct Billing support, geography, token coverage and local-currency settlement apply to direct Crypto. Link has its own eligibility and settlement scope.
